phase: Increment 0 = AC1+AC2 (defect quick wins); Increment 1 = AC3+AC4 (census + explainer); Increment 2 = AC5 (Max design-review gate — ratify or amend; amendments fold into this contract before building on); Increment 3 = AC6+AC7+AC8 (uniqueness + revisit stability, against the ratified scheme)

acceptanceCriteria.statement: IC434 (Horsehead) and M78 no longer share a galacticPos in KnownObjectProfiles; both survive the known-object injection dedup; the Horsehead actually renders in the galaxy.

verifyVia.input: Headless: run the known-object injection over the profile catalog. Live: navigate to IC434's corrected position.
verifyVia.observable: Injection output contains BOTH IC434 and M78 at distinct positions (the SHADOWED=['IC434'] special-case is deleted from tests/known-object-feature-seed.test.js, which still passes); live, a nebula renders at IC434's position.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The 4 pre-existing failures in src/generation/__tests__ (KnownObjects x3, GalacticFeatures x1) pass, tightened to the 37-profile catalog — not loosened.

verifyVia.observable: 0 failures; assertions reference the actual catalog (no length-5 relics; the 'ring' and 'pleiades' searches disambiguated to their intended profiles).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A committed, re-runnable headless census generates system names at volumes far beyond player reach across all four region buckets (core/arm/rim/halo) and reports duplicate rates per naming path (catalog / Greek / fantasy-word), including collisions against the ~15.6k real HYG designations, plus emits name samples at volume for Max's review.

verifyVia.input: Run the census tool twice (exact command documented in the tool header).
verifyVia.observable: A report with per-path, per-region duplicate rates + at least 200 name samples per region; the two runs are byte-identical (seeded, deterministic).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An explainer doc gives Max the in-depth picture: how each naming path works (catalog/fantasy split percentages, syllable tables, sectorCode hash, region flavor, forked seed streams), how all FOUR real-object tagging mechanisms work (KnownSystems, RealStarCatalog, KnownObjectProfiles, RealFeatureCatalog), what real name/characteristic data flows into the game on each targeting path (including the sky-click vs NavComputer naming split), with census numbers cited and claims pointing at code.

verifyVia.input: Read the doc; spot-check its code citations against the source.
verifyVia.observable: Doc exists under docs/, covers every enumerated section, citations resolve to real code; the docs/SYSTEMS.md 'no doc yet' rows (data-catalogs, generation-style, generation-system) now point to it.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Max, from the census report, samples, and explainer, is happy with the proc gen naming system — he ratifies the scheme (style split, formats, regional flavor) or specifies amendments, in his words.

verifyVia.input: Max reviews the AC3 report + AC4 doc.
verifyVia.observable: A ratify-or-amend decision recorded in this workstream directory; amendments (if any) folded into this contract via the scope skill before AC6/AC7 build.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Players never encounter the same system name twice: at census volumes (>=100k generated systems across regions), distinct systems produce zero duplicate names, and procgen names never collide with real HYG catalog designations.

verifyVia.input: Re-run the AC3 census against the post-fix generator.
verifyVia.observable: 0 duplicates among distinct systems; 0 procgen names matching real catalog designations; the mechanism is by-construction or registry-backed, not luck (the report states which).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Re-visiting a system gives back the same name on EVERY targeting path: names derive from stable identity (position/seed), never transient starfield indices; sky-click and NavComputer targeting of the same star agree on its name (for real stars, the catalog name).

verifyVia.input: Live: click-target the same star before and after starfield regeneration and warp in twice; separately target the same real star via sky-click vs NavComputer.
verifyVia.observable: Identical system name across both visits and across both targeting paths; real stars show their catalog name on the sky-click path too.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Sol still resolves as Sol with its known-system contents and real planet names (always-test-Sol: Sol IS the known-system code path).

verifyVia.input: Boot into / warp to Sol in the running game.
verifyVia.observable: System name 'Sol'; real planet names (Mercury through Neptune) present; no procgen name leakage anywhere in the system.
